title: Tunes at the parade, syncopated marches and Dave Perkins's sheet music
summary: Laine can recall only a break and the march 'Underarm' that Perkins brought; they ragged straight marches like Stars and Stripes Forever.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: By God, it's wonderful. Can you remember how any of those tunes go that you played at that political parade? Can you hum any of them?
Well, not in particular, but there's one of them that had a break in it. La la. La la. La La
La I say, if you syncopate a march, it comes out a rag. That's all. Yeah. You play a march hard, it's a rag.

Now, we used to play that underarm march. That was a wonderful march. Dave Perkins came down one night with a copy of that. And Dave Perkins was a first-class note reader. Really. That boy could take a sheet of music and go over it like nobody's business. Is that right? Well, he'd hum it. He'd hum it to the bunch. And the kids, man, they said they had a ear for music. Every one of them. Every one of them had a ear for music. Well, first thing you know, they start. They play this stuff, try to play it. Then he tried to manage to teach them and show them, you know. Well, we went along. Now, we used to play that underarm march. Underarm march is the name of it? Underarm.
That's the name of the march. Then we played another march. Nethermarch is something about the American flag or something like that. I can't remember that stuff no more. It's been too long.
Right. Ask him if he ever heard the Stars and Stripes forever. I can't remember it. Did you ever hear the Stars and Stripes forever? Yes. We played that. You did? We played that. Did you rag it up?
Yes, we rag it up. We tear it up. Yes, we tear it up. Could dance. All of that stuff, that straight stuff, you understand? Right. All that straight stuff, we'd rag it up.
Of course, we should go. Well, I'll be there.
I mean, we should go. Yeah.
And that was for the political meeting that you played when you were 14. Yeah.
Well, actually, good after I was 14, I was around, I must have been close to 15 years old. I see. I must have been close to 15 years old when that happened.
